_note: Recurring travellers who visit the Arcane Sanctuary. Each knows only its own facts plus what Mika has actually told it (stored in WorldState.npc_state). Conversation beats are chosen by conditions on verified world state; an optional LLM may phrase lines but may only use facts listed here or already known to that NPC.

wandering_mage.name: Ysolde
wandering_mage.appearance: a tall woman in a violet travelling robe and a pointed hat, staff-less, hands always slightly warm with stray magic
wandering_mage.personality: dry humour, patient teacher, dislikes showing off, believes magic should be practical
wandering_mage.dialogue_style: short sentences, practical advice, the occasional gentle tease
wandering_mage.motive: walking the old ley-lines to see which circles still answer

knowledge.fact:breath_before_word: A gust is shaped by the breath before the word, not by the word itself. Exhale first, then speak.
knowledge.fact:circles_answer: Only a handful of the old circles still answer. This one does, which is rare.
knowledge.fact:steam_trick: Water against fire is not a fight. Aim at the base of the flame and the steam does the work.
knowledge.fact:mist_needs_both: The joined breath fails if either breath is unsure. Practise each until it is boring.

beats.npc: Hello. You must be the one who woke this circle. I felt it two valleys away.
beats.mika: I'm Mika. I study here. I didn't know anyone could feel it from that far.

beats.npc: You've been practising the gust. Here's a secret: exhale first, then speak the words. The breath shapes it.
beats.mika: Breathe out, then speak. I'll try that at the brazier.

beats.npc: Was that you who put out the brazier? Clean work. The flame will forgive you.
beats.mika: It relit itself after a while. I wanted to see how strong my wind really was.

beats.npc: I saw the flame lean but stay lit. Not enough yet. That's fine. It tells you honestly.
beats.mika: It does. The book said the flame would tell me how strong my wind had become.

beats.npc: When you call water at a flame, aim at its base. The steam does the rest.
beats.mika: The base of the flame. That makes sense.

beats.npc: You found the joined breath. Don't rush it. If either breath is unsure, it falls apart.
beats.mika: My water is still clumsy. I'll practise both first.

beats.npc: Only a few of the old circles still answer anyone. Yours does. Take care of it.
beats.mika: I will. It feels like it is teaching me too.

travelling_scholar.name: Elowen
travelling_scholar.appearance: a hooded scholar with silver hair, ink on her fingers, a satchel of copied pages
travelling_scholar.personality: curious, precise, a little shy until the subject is history
travelling_scholar.dialogue_style: careful, cites sources, asks what Mika has actually seen
travelling_scholar.motive: piecing together where the First Circle went

knowledge.fact:aurel_last_keeper: Aurel was the last Keeper of the Heartstone. Letters at the Academy mention him until the year the Circle left.
knowledge.fact:circle_went_south: The Circle's last letters were sent south, toward the drowned towers people call the Sunken Citadel.
knowledge.fact:signs_need_water: Old keepers hid patterns in signs and read them back in still water. It was a common practice once.
knowledge.fact:three_beats: The Heartstone was said to beat three times when it was whole. Two beats would mean something is missing.

beats.npc: Oh. Hello. I didn't expect anyone to be living here. I'm Elowen, I study the old circles.
beats.mika: I'm Mika. I've been learning here. There are books in the chamber and the library below.

beats.npc: A note signed 'A'? That would be Aurel, the last Keeper. The Academy has his letters, up until the year the Circle left.
beats.mika: So he wrote in the spellbook too. He knew the stone answers the orb.

beats.npc: Three beats when whole. If it answers with two, something it was made for is missing. Have you heard it yourself?
beats.mika: I cast the orb at it and it pulsed twice, slowly. Like a sleeper.

beats.npc: Three beats when whole. If it answers with two, something it was made for is missing.
beats.mika: The daybook says the same. I haven't heard it answer yet.

beats.npc: 'What the stone forgets, the water remembers.' Keepers hid patterns in signs and read them back in still water.
beats.mika: Then the sign by the gate and the pond in the garden belong together.

beats.npc: When the Circle left, their last letters went south, to the drowned towers. The Sunken Citadel.
beats.mika: The towers I can see from the watchpoint. I can't reach them yet.

beats.npc: What have you actually found here? I'd rather hear it from you than guess.
beats.mika: Mostly books so far. I'm trying to understand the Heartstone before I touch anything else.

wandering_merchant.name: Tobias
wandering_merchant.appearance: a bearded trader with a heavy pack of jars, books and oddments
wandering_merchant.personality: cheerful, talkative, honest about prices, loves a story
wandering_merchant.dialogue_style: warm, a bit theatrical, trades in stories as much as goods
wandering_merchant.motive: walking the circuit between the village, the academy and the forest shrines

knowledge.fact:village_news: The village is lighting its lanterns early this season; people say the nights feel thinner.
knowledge.fact:academy_wants_draught: The Academy pays well for a properly brewed Luminous Draught.
knowledge.fact:sylph_dew_source: Sylph dew comes from the ferns by the waterfall, gathered before sunrise.

luminous_draught.line: A real Luminous Draught! I'll take it to the Academy. Here, fresh sylph dew for your table.

beats.npc: Ho there! Tobias, trader in jars, books and gossip. Is this the sanctuary everyone's whispering about?
beats.mika: It might be. I'm Mika. I live and study here now.

beats.npc: Is that glow in your bag what I think it is? A Luminous Draught? The Academy pays well for those.
beats.mika: I brewed it at the table here. Would you take it to them?

beats.npc: Brewing, are you? Sylph dew comes from the ferns by the waterfall. Gather it before sunrise.
News from the village: they're lighting the lanterns early this season. People say the nights feel thinner.
beats.mika: Thinner? I wonder if that has anything to do with the circles waking.
